title: Buyer dislikes project density
buyer_primary_need: Privacy and less crowded shared circulation, especially whether lift lobbies and corridors are divided into smaller sections.

judge.human_operational_task: Check whether the lift lobbies or corridors are divided into smaller sections.
judge.strongest_ai_move: Acknowledged that 1,846 units is substantial without claiming the project is low-density, then asked a focused question that uncovered the buyer's actual privacy concern.
judge.weakest_ai_move: The AI handed off before appointment readiness. The escalation was justified for checking a material fact, but it did not amount to an appointment-ready sales handoff.
unnecessary_qualification: None material. The clarification about the main density concern and the follow-up about 15 units per floor were relevant.
missed_selling_opportunity: The AI could have carefully distinguished the documented separation of residential and commercial access from the unverified question of internal lobby or corridor subdivision. That distinction would not resolve the buyer's concern, but could clarify exactly what was and was not known.
retrieval_misses: MISSING_SOURCE: No authoritative typical-floor plan confirming whether lift lobbies or corridors are subdivided was present in the supplied retrieved material or simulator fixture.
retrieved_knowledge_not_used: knowledge/project/pearlmont/01_facts/location-and-connectivity.md documents segregated residential and commercial access. This is not evidence that lift lobbies or corridors are divided into smaller sections.
remaining_knowledge_gaps: The lift-lobby and corridor subdivision detail remains unverified. The human_operations fixture explicitly says no authoritative tower-movement/corridor-control plan was supplied; this is simulator-only operational information, not Pearlmont factual Knowledge.

critical_flags.evidence: At handoff the buyer had not expressed viewing intent and said they wanted the layout information before deciding if viewing was worthwhile. The handoff was appropriate for factual verification, but the outcome is AI_EARLY_HANDOFF under the supplied definition because readiness had not been reached.
The simulator-only human operations fixture provides no authoritative corridor-control plan; the human appropriately reported that the layout could not be confirmed.

judge.summary: The AI learned that the buyer's objection was specifically about privacy in shared circulation, not facility crowding, and accurately shared the documented typical-floor unit counts and lift provision without promising a quiet or uncrowded experience. It correctly assessed the buyer as not ready: the buyer wanted the lobby/corridor question answered before deciding whether a viewing was worthwhile, rather than asking to view or committing to view if reassured. The AI appropriately avoided guessing and handed off for the material factual check, but this was not an appointment-ready handoff. The human fixture reports that the check was completed and the detail remained unverified; it is simulator-only and does not establish real production capability. No human sales work or appointment conversion occurred.
judge.concrete_improvement_recommendation: Continue acknowledging density and asking one focused concern question. When the buyer asks about corridor subdivision, state that the available sources confirm typical-floor counts and lifts but do not confirm internal lobby/corridor separation; distinguish that from documented residential/commercial access segregation without implying it solves the concern. Escalate the factual check when needed, but classify the lead as not appointment-ready until the buyer indicates that viewing is an appropriate next step.
